JUDGMENT Heard Shri Prakasha H.C., learned counsel for the appellant as well as Shri K. Suresh, learned counsel who is representing Respondent No.2.

Despite service of notice, none appears for Respondent No.1.
2.

Challenge in this appeal is the order that is rendered by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal,
Mandya, in MVC No.39/2015 dated 11.03.2019.
As against the claim for Rs.50,00,000/- by the claimant / appellant, the Tribunal through the impugned order, awarded a sum of Rs.10,85,996/- as compensation.
Aggrieved by the sum NC: 2024:KHC:20712-DB awarded and seeking for enhancement of compensation, the present appeal is preferred.
3. Arguing in respect of the merits of the matter, learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant sustained grievous injuries due to the accident and became permanently disabled.
The appellant was working as a Cook under a Caterer and was eking out his livelihood.
But due to the injuries sustained, more particularly to the temporal bone, he is unable to do any work and thereby he is dependant on others.
Learned counsel also submits that the appellant incurred huge amount towards medical expenses and the Doctor assessed the disability as 40%.
However, the Tribunal though considered the entire evidence, went wrong in taking the whole body disability as 10%.
Learned counsel further contends that the amount awarded as compensation under all other heads is also improper and inadequate and hence, the compensation granted requires enhancement.

Per contra, learned counsel for Respondent No.2 states that the Tribunal has examined the case and discussed at length about the occupation and income of the appellant by the date of accident and further, the disability aspect was also taken into consideration and thereby the Tribunal is right S Pratheesha vs Sudhindra Shekar on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74886072/
2 in awarding a sum of Rs.10,85,996/- as compensation and hence the award of the Tribunal needs no interference.

sentences.text: 5. However, learned counsel for Respondent No.2 graciously submits that instead of taking the notional income of the appellant as Rs.8,000/- per month, the Tribunal ought to have taken his income as Rs.8,500/- per month, which figure is considered even by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority while calculating the compensation.

6. The Tribunal through the impugned order, has awarded compensation divided under different heads as under:
NC: 2024:KHC:20712-DB 1
Towards pain and sufferings Rs. 50,000/- 2
Towards medical expenses Rs.7,66,196 + and future medical expenses 30,000/- 3

Towards attendant charges, Rs. 21,000/-
conveyance, nursing care, nourishment and towards other incidental expenses 4

Towards loss of income during Rs. 16,000/-
laid down period 5

Towards loss of future income Rs. 1,72,800/-
due to permanent disability 6

Towards physical disability Rs. 30,000/-
affecting future amenities in the life of the petitioner TOTAL Rs.10,85,996/-
7.
A perusal of record reveals that the appellant sustained fracture of occipital bone and commuted fracture of left Clavicle.
The Doctor opined that both the injuries sustained are grievous in nature.

Further, there is no dispute of the fact that the appellant took treatment as in- patient from 28.09.2014 to 17.10.2014 and also from 01.12.2014 to 04.12.2014 at Columbia Asia Hospital,
Mysore.
Equally, it is not in dispute that the appellant underwent surgery for fixation of left clavicle fracture and further he underwent bone flap replacement procedure.
The appellant undertook treatment as in-patient for a total period of 24 days.
8. Having considered these aspects, the Tribunal came to a conclusion that the amount that can be awarded under the head 'Pain and suffering' for the injuries sustained is Rs.50,000/-.

However, we are of the considered view that having regard to the grievous injuries sustained, that too as one of the injury is at occipital region, it would be just and reasonable to award Rs.80,000/- under the head 'Pain and suffering'.

Likewise, the Tribunal though awarded a sum of Rs.21,000/- towards 'Attendant charges, conveyance charges, Nursing care, nourishment and other incidental expenses',
having considered the fact that the appellant took extensive treatment as in-patient twice,
underwent two surgical procedures and was taking follow up treatment, this Court is of the view that under all those heads, a sum of Rs.30,000/- is required to be awarded.

The Tribunal, taking the notional income as Rs.8,000/- per month, awarded a sum of Rs.16,000/- as compensation towards S Pratheesha vs Sudhindra Shekar on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74886072/
3 NC: 2024:KHC:20712-DB 'Loss of income during laid up period', taking the laid-up period to be two months.

However, considering the fact that the appellant was taking treatment as in-patient for long period of 24 days and that he sustained fracture of his clavicle bone and also grievous injuries at his occipital region, we are of the view that the appellant would not have been in a position to attend his normal pursuits at least for a period of six months.
Taking the notional income of Rs.8,500/- per month, 'Loss of income during laid-up period' for six months, comes to Rs.51,000/-.

This Court does not find any reason to interfere with the award of medical expenses of Rs.7,66,196/- and also Rs.30,000/- towards 'future medical expenses'.
9.

Coming to the aspect of 'Loss of future income due to permanent disability', the Tribunal having assessed the disability as 10% in respect of the whole body, taking the notional income as Rs.8,000/-, applying the appropriate multiplier '18', has awarded a sum of Rs.1,72,800/- towards 'Loss of income due to disability'.

However, having considered the nature of injuries sustained and NC: 2024:KHC:20712-DB more particularly taking into consideration the assessment of functional disability by the Doctor who examined the appellant and the contents of Exhibit C5, we are of the view that functional disability in respect of the whole body can be taken as 15%.

Therefore, taking the notional income as Rs.8,500/-, keeping the appropriate multiplier as '18' intact with the percentage of disability as 15%, the 'Loss of future earnings due to disability', comes to Rs.2,75,400/-.
10. The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.30,000/- towards loss sustained which affects future amenities in life.
There is nothing to interfere with the said amount awarded.

Thus, the total compensation which the appellant would be entitled under different heads would be as under:
Sl.No.
Heads of compensation
Amount awarded 1 Pain and suffering Rs. 80,000/- 2
Medical expenses Rs. 7,66,196/- 3

Future medical expenses Rs. 30,000/-
NC: 2024:KHC:20712-DB 4 Attendant charges, conveyance charges, nursing Rs. 30,000/- care,
nourishment and other incidental expenses 5 Loss of income during laid-up Rs. 51,000/-
period 6 Loss of future income due to Rs. 2,75,400/-
permanent disability 7

Physical disability which affects Rs. 30,000/-
the future amenities in life Rs.12,62,596/-
TOTAL AMOUNT 11.

In the light of the foregoing discussion, we pass the following:
ORDER i) The appeal is allowed in part.

iii) The enhanced sum shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
